slides.heading: Cappuccino is breakfast.
paragraphs: For Italians, a cappuccino is a morning ritual — usually with a cornetto, standing at the bar counter.
After lunch or dinner? Order one and you'll get a polite smile… and a very Italian look.

slides.heading: It's all about digestion.
paragraphs: Many Italians believe that a big cup of hot milk after a meal feels heavy and slows digestion.
Science may debate it. Italian grandmothers do not.

slides.heading: What to ask for instead
items: A shot of espresso. In Italy, “caffè” is espresso.
Espresso “stained” with a drop of milk foam.
Espresso “corrected” with a splash of grappa.

slides.heading: Don't say “espresso”.
paragraphs: At the bar, just say: “Un caffè, per favore.”
Three words. Instant Italian citizenship. (Not legally.)

slides.title: Save it for your next trip.
slides.text: Follow for Italian Rule Nº 2 — and confess: how many cappuccinos after lunch?

caption:
Italian Rule Nº 1 ☕
Never order a cappuccino after 11 a.m.

In Italy, cappuccino is a breakfast ritual. After a meal, Italians switch to a simple “caffè” — and yes, that means espresso.

Have you ever broken this rule? This is a safe space. Mostly 👇

—
🇮🇹 Regola italiana n.1: mai un cappuccino dopo le 11. Voi la rispettate davvero?
